messages:
Alex W: Heads-up — saw a P95 tail spike in canary this morning when routing through the multi-variant pool (mix of q4 and fp16). Not huge, but consistent across 3 runs.
Maya R: saw that too. Looks like batch formation is fragmenting when variants have different compat sets. small batches + frequent fallbacks.
Samir: I pulled the coalescer logs. We're forming a lot of tiny batches (1-3 requests) instead of merging to the token_budget. suspect queue_policy merge window too tight.
Samir: snippet from the logs:
```
[batcher] formed_batch id=0 size=2 target_tokens=32 accumulated_tokens=3 compat_set=mv_set_9
[batcher] flush reason=timeout merge_window_ms=6
```
Ryan L: kv stats for same run look rough — kv_misses are spiking right when fallbacks occur. thrash + kernel selection churn = extra overhead.
perf-bot: nightly-profile 1923456000 -> canary P95 +18% vs baseline. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/1923456000 (permissioned).
Alex W: two hypotheses: (1) permissive merging across compat sets is letting incompatible variants coalesce then trigger fallback, which forces small flushes; (2) kernel selection per-request is adding CPU/GPU overhead when variants switch mid-batch.
Maya R: Agreed. We should try: increase merge_window_ms, and add a compat-aware merge heuristic that prefers same-compat merges. Also consider bumping token_budget for small requests.
Samir: quick experiment idea — change queue_policy to:
```
queue_policy:
  merge_window_ms: 25
  token_budget: 48
  allow_cross_compat_merge: false
```
Run on one canary pool and watch batch sizes + kv hit rate.
Ryan L: Also add a lightweight per-variant KV warmup (first N requests pinned to variant) to reduce immediate miss rate when a fallback happens. That should lower the short-term cost of fallbacks.
Maya R: note: kernel selection cache currently keyed by (model_variant, seq_len). If we frequently switch variants inside the same worker we lose kernel locality. Maybe extend kernel cache TTL or bias routing to keep variant stickiness per-worker.
Samir: reproduced locally with the repro script: `python tools/repro_batching.py --variants 3 --mix q4,fp16 --load 120rps` — it created many flushes at merge_window_ms=8. Increasing merge_window_ms to 20 doubled median batch size.
Alex W: Can someone file a small canary config PR and run it tonight? We want metrics: batch_size distribution, P95 latency, kv_hit/miss, kernel_switch_count.
Ryan L: I'll add KV metrics to the canary dashboard tile. Samir — can you paste the exact repro command and the minimal config change?
Samir: repro command: `python tools/repro_batching.py --profile --variants 3 --qps 120 --request_len_dist short`
Samir: minimal config: set `merge_window_ms=20`, `token_budget=48`, `prefer_same_compat=true` (new flag for coalescer).
Maya R: will draft the PR. also propose an A/B: permissive merge (current) vs compat-aware merge. Run 4h each.
Alex W: thanks. Action items: PR for canary (Maya), kv dashboard tile (Ryan), repro + logs (Samir). I'll follow up with a quick post-canary summary. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note — flagging related alerts: batcher_flush_rate_up and kv_miss_rate_up for canary pool 7.
Ryan L: ping me if you want me to run a nightly run with increased token_budget and warmup.
Alex W: will coordinate. End of thread.
